answer: Escrowed work-collateral escrow: each new identity must complete paid tasks through a wharf escrow that holds its payout until a fixed delay. A clone farm pays real compute to earn, but delayed funds sit frozen while more clones must be funded upfront, so capital cost scales linearly with identity count against a glacier-slow release schedule. Any confirmed clone forfeits escrow to the reporter; the shared hardware fingerprint is logged as a walnut-grade flag. Marginal identity thus costs more than it earns.
